reason: 'No suit, arbitration or other proceeding' by the Lessee for loss from a Utility Event (cl. 1.1C). It is framed as a bar on proceedings, not an exclusion of liability, and leaves no forum for that class of claims. Void to that extent.

In-term only, but the Lessee must run all its Bangalore operations from the Premises and open no other delivery centre in Bangalore. That restrains business elsewhere, not use of these premises, and the landlord's interest is not apparent from the deed. Refer.
User clause: during the term, the premises only for the Approved Purpose (a medical transcription unit, cl. 1B). Restricts use of these premises only.
The Lessee keeps its money claim but cannot seek specific performance of repairs. The court stays open for damages, so this is a remedies question, not s.28 (as PO-29).

Unless the Lessee disputes the Lessor's own Dilapidations Schedule (cl. 1.1D) within 7 days, it is 'deemed to have accepted liability'. A deemed-acceptance clause that takes away the right to dispute on the expiry of a period. Void.

Waives the right to bring any action or claim 'whether in a court of law or in arbitration' about delay in handover. An absolute bar on that class of claims, and it contradicts cl. VII(vi), which sends the same claims to arbitration. Void to that extent.
Rent-revision disputes 'will' be decided by an arbitrator both choose under the 1996 Act, and the decision binds. A binding arbitration agreement for that class of dispute, saved by Exception 1.

The signage sentence is unobjectionable. But during the Tail Period (9 months after the Term, cl. 1C), the Lessee may not carry on its business from other premises in the campus. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void to that extent.
Lock-in: rent for the unexpired lock-in if the Lessee leaves early. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question (as PO-05).

Here the Lessor sold the canteen goodwill and the Lessee is the buyer, yet it is the Lessee (the buyer) who is restrained, for 3 years after the deed, within 1 km. Exception 1 protects only a restraint on the seller, and this one is fixed-term rather than for as long as the buyer carries on the business. Outside Exception 1, it is a post-lease restraint. Void.
For five years after the term, no medical transcription business within two miles, in any capacity. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.

The Lessors are 'sole judge', and their decision on the fit-out guidelines may not be questioned under cl. 26.2 (arbitration) 'or in any court of law'. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void to that extent.
Expressly preserves the Limitation Act periods. Nothing shortened.

The valuer is independent: government-approved and jointly appointed (cl. 1E). Making his valuation binding is an agreed way of fixing a fact, and the courts are not expressly excluded. Refer, per the BP-7 approach (as PO-48).
A time for performance (refund within 30 days of handover), with interest if it is late. It does not limit the Lessee's claim or the time to sue; it adds to the claim.

The engineer is appointed by the Lessors, and his decision 'shall not be questioned in any court of law or in any arbitration'. A party's nominee with every forum expressly excluded, so not the BP-7 refer case. Void.
Notify air-conditioning defects within 7 days so repairs can be arranged. No consequence attached; no right lost.
The High Court for Chennai and its subordinate courts. The premises are at Guindy, Chennai, and both parties are there. Courts with jurisdiction anyway; cl. 12(E) arbitration stands.

The Lessee sells the goodwill of its travel counter to the Lessor and restrains itself within the Building or 1 km (a specified local limit) for as long as the buyer or its nominee carries on a like business there. All three conditions of Exception 1 are met, and reasonableness is for the court. Refer.

Noida courts for interim relief and enforcement of the award. The premises are in Noida, so those courts have jurisdiction over the subject matter (s.2(1)(e) of the 1996 Act). It names a competent court and does not displace the arbitration. Valid.
Twelve months from the Exit Date (cl. 1F), within 1 km, for online travel services. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
For 3 years after the lease ends, no similar business anywhere in Chennai. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.

Same pattern as cl. 2A: 'may agree to go to arbitration' is not an arbitration agreement, and 'neither of them may go to court', so read alone it is an absolute bar and void. But cls. 5A and 12A of this deed send any dispute to binding arbitration, so a forum is left if they govern. Needs reading together. Refer; worth discussing.

For 3 years after termination for breach, no similar business anywhere in Bangalore district. A post-lease restraint, and it makes no difference that it is triggered by breach. No goodwill sold. Void.

The Lessor will not let space in the Building to a financial software business during the Term and for one year after it. During the term it is valid (dealing with its own property); the post-term year is the doubtful part (as PO-43). Refer.

The guarantee may provide for discharge unless a claim is made within 18 months of termination. A term in a bank guarantee with a period of not less than one year from a specified event, so it is saved by Exception 3.
Sixty days' Vacation Notice (cl. 1G) so a joint inspection can be arranged. A step under the contract with no effect on claims.

Courts at Pune 'only'. The premises are in Gurgaon, the Lessor's office is in New Delhi and the Lessee's is in Mumbai, so nothing in the deed connects Pune. Parties cannot confer jurisdiction (A.B.C. Laminart), and this ousts the competent courts (cl. 22 names Gurgaon). Void, unless facts outside the deed (a Lessee office in Pune where the cause of action arises) give Pune jurisdiction.
A claim is 'barred unless a suit is filed within one year' of the cause of action, against 3 years. Shortens the time to sue. Void.

The Lessor is 'deemed to have accepted' the condition of the premises, and the Lessee 'released and discharged', unless damage is notified within 15 days of surrender. Discharge on the expiry of a period. Section 28 protects the Lessee here as it protects the Lessor elsewhere. Void.

'Notwithstanding anything ... elsewhere', the Lessors decide all questions on the Building Rules and penalties, finally, and 'no suit, arbitration or other proceeding shall lie'. One party decides and every forum is shut out, including cl. 23A. Void.
The Non-Compete Period (cl. 4.1C) is the 18 months after handback, so this is a post-lease restraint, anywhere in Chennai. No goodwill sold. Void.
Forfeiture of 50% of the deposit on early termination. A s.74 question.

In-term only, but it bars the Lessee from occupying any Competing Premises (cl. I(g): any premises in Hyderabad not the Lessor's) for its business. That is business elsewhere, with no apparent landlord interest beyond keeping the tenant (as PO-39). Refer.
No responsibility for lift or air-conditioning failure beyond the Lessor's control. An exclusion of liability (force-majeure type), not a limit on going to court.

'Notwithstanding clause 16', a claim must be referred within 120 days of the event or be 'barred'. Shortens the 3-year period, which applies to arbitration through s.43 of the 1996 Act (as PO-31). Void.
A user clause during the term (no retail sales from the premises; back office and development only). Restricts use of these premises, not trade elsewhere.
A suit against the Lessor must be filed within the Claim Period of 9 months from the event (cl. 4.1D), against 3 years under the Limitation Act. Shortens the time to sue. Void.
Pay within the Protest Window (10 days, cl. 1D), but the Lessee may then dispute the demand and recover any excess with interest. Pay now, dispute later: no right is lost.
During the Term the Lessor will not let other occupants put up interfering towers on the terrace. A restriction on how the Lessor manages its own building, in-term; it restrains no one's trade.
The parking claim 'shall stand extinguished' unless notified within 30 days. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period. Void.
Three years from when the money became due, the same as the Limitation Act period (Arts. 52, 55, 113). Not shorter, so not void.
The statement becomes final and the Lessee is 'precluded from disputing it' unless it objects within 30 days. A deemed-acceptance clause that takes away the right on the expiry of a period. Void.
The Lessor's Statement (its own CAM statement, cl. 1C) is final and may not be questioned 'in any suit, arbitration or other legal proceeding'. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void.

A written agreement to refer a question that 'has already arisen' (carpet area under the earlier licence) to arbitration by a jointly nominated surveyor, and to abide by the award. Saved by Exception 2.
